newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier unit gets C$34 mln rail order.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier unit gets C$34 mln rail order.

text.p: Bombardier Inc said on Wednesday that its French Subsidiary ANF-Industrie received a C$34 million option order for the supply of double-deck rail vehicles.

The order from the Societe Nationale des Chemins de Fer de France (SNCF) was part of a C$100 million contract awarded to ANF-Industrie, based in Crespin, France, and GEC Alsthom to manufacture and supply of 16 TER2N electric multiple units.
Each unit consists of a two-car double-deck train set designed for regional passenger transport, and includes a motorized unit and a trailer.
ANF-Industrie and GEC Alsthom were chosen in November 1995 for a partnership in the construction of the TER2N.

The original contract was for the delivery of 76 multiple units, which included the option of 16 multiple units, for a total value of 2 billion francs (C$470 million). ANF-Industrie's share of the whole contract amounts to 734 million francs (C$173 million), Bombardier said.
ANF-Industrie is responsible for the manufacture of the trailers and motorized bogies, while GEC Alsthom builds the motorized units and the traction equipment.
The first TER2N delivery is scheduled for September 1997 and the total order is expected to be completed by November 1999.
ANF-Industrie is part of Bombardier's Transportation Group, based in Saint-Bruno, Quebec. ((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
